steps.t: Set up accounts: YouTube channel, TikTok, Facebook page, Instagram
steps.d: One gaming name/handle across all four. Turn on 2FA.

steps.t: Sign up for Higgsfield and open Content Factory
Find 3 viral GTA clips to use as reference videos
steps.d: Search YouTube for “GTA gameplay”, sort by views. Save the ones whose visual style you like.

steps.t: Save your prompt and template (Recreate template)
steps.d: Paste the prompt into the How to clip tab so it’s one tap away.

steps.t: Practice batch: 5 clips from GTA V gameplay
steps.d: Set minutes + episode count, generate, check hooks and captions.

steps.t: Post the practice batch on all 4 platforms
steps.d: Learn the upload flow now, not on launch day.
Map reveal, first heist, cars, Lucia/Jason, glitches, “things you missed”.

steps.t: Launch day: post first GTA 6 clips within hours
steps.d: Speed beats polish on day one.

steps.t: Post 3+ clips a day across every platform
steps.d: Log each one in the Clip log.

steps.t: Check which hooks get views; make more of those
Apply for monetization as each platform qualifies
steps.d: YouTube Partner Program, TikTok Creator Rewards, Facebook content monetization.

steps.t: Decide: keep going daily, or fold into the Faceless YouTube project

steps: Go to YouTube and search GTA gameplay. Note the views these videos get.
Add a reference video for its visual style, then hit Recreate template.
Paste in your prompt (the creator’s is in her pinned comment).
Set the minutes and the episode number (how many clips to make).
In a few minutes you get videos you can post to YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Facebook Reels and get monetized.
pay: Short-form pays per view, not per clip. Payouts vary by platform, country and niche, and change often.
YouTube Shorts: ad-revenue share after you join the Partner Program.
TikTok: Creator Rewards pays only on videos over 1 minute.
Facebook Reels: content monetization program, invite-based.
how.warn: Copyright: clipping someone else’s YouTube gameplay can get claimed or struck. Your own captured gameplay is safest. Rockstar generally allows gameplay videos, but reuploaded footage from other creators is not yours.
